title: Dedicated capacity: load scenario suite + regression detector
creator: Anika Shah
description:
Overview:
We need a repeatable, automated suite for Dedicated capacity soak and autoscaling scenarios that measures tokens/sec throughput, p95 tail latency, and detects regressions automatically across bursts and steady-state workloads. This ticket designs and implements the harness, a statistical regression detector, dashboards, and CI gating for model/runtime upgrades on Dedicated pools.

Goals:
- Provide a set of canonical load profiles (burst, steady-state, ramp, noisy-burst) that reflect production traffic composition and sequence-length distribution.
- Measure tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, and queue depth.
- Implement a regression detector that flags meaningful degradations (configurable thresholds + statistical test) and opens a PR/alert.
- Validate autoscaling policies under 1x, 2x, and 3x sudden load and prolonged soak at 70% capacity for 6 hours.
- Add dashboards and Datadog/Grafana monitors with clear runbooks.

Success metrics (target thresholds for acceptance):
- Steady-state tokens/sec within ±6% of baseline for 6-hour soak at target concurrency.
- p95 increase < 20% relative to baseline; p99 must not exceed 2x baseline for steady-state.
- Burst recovery time (time to return to p95 within 10% of baseline) < 90s after 3x traffic spike.
- Regression detector false positive rate < 2% over a 30-day historic run.

Test matrix (initial):
- Profile A (Quick burst): 30s spike to 3x RPS, then back to baseline. Run 30 iterations.
- Profile B (Short ramp): linear ramp from 0.2x to 2.5x over 10 minutes, hold 10 minutes, then ramp down.
- Profile C (Steady soak): sustained 70% capacity for 6 hours to exercise KV cache and batching warm paths.
- Profile D (Noisy-burst): Poisson arrivals with heavy-tailed sequence lengths, 4% error injection for transient infra faults.

Harness design notes:
- Client: new "soak-runner" microservice (Go) that can run k6-compatible scripts and emit OpenTelemetry traces + Prometheus metrics.
- Workload definition stored as YAML in repo so CI can parameterize runs per pool size.
- Warmup: mandatory 15-minute warmup to populate KV cache and reach steady batching. Warmup is excluded from metric windows.
- Traffic mix: derive proportions from anonymized production sampling weekly; default mix uses 60% short prompts (<64 tokens), 30% medium (64-512), 10% long (>512).
- Hooks: ability to inject model variants and quantization profiles to validate fallbacks and kernel changes.

Regression detection algorithm:
- Baseline: rolling 7-day median for each measurable (tokens/sec, p95) per pool size and model family stored in S3 as time series snapshots.
- Detector: dual checks: (1) absolute threshold breach (e.g., tokens/sec drop >8% OR p95 increase >25%), and (2) statistical check using two-sample bootstrap on recent-bucket vs baseline with 95% CI. Both must pass to trigger a regression alert to reduce noise.
- Drift handling: uses EWMA with alpha=0.2 to smooth benign upward or downward drift; manual baseline re-acceptance window for infra upgrades.
- Auto-noise suppression: if traffic variance high (CV>0.25) apply higher thresholds for p95 to avoid false positives during bursts.

Alerting / dashboards / CI gating:
- Datadog monitors: tokens-per-sec-monitored (alert-level: P0) and p95-latency-regression (alert-level: P1). PagerDuty integration for P0.
- Grafana dashboard: dedicated/soak-suite overview (tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99, error rate, queue depth, GPU utilization). Dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood/company/dashboards/dedicated-soak-suite
- CI gating: a GitHub Action will run quick-scan (Profile A+B) on PRs touching runtime or kernels. Full soak (Profile C) is nightly and must pass with no regression flags before release promotion to runtime-1.22. PR example: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/211

Acceptance criteria:
- Harness service merged behind feature flag and runnable via k8s job with documented config.
- At least one 6-hour steady soak executed against a staging Dedicated pool with logged tokens/sec and p95 showing stable values within thresholds. Upload results to S3.
- Regression detector runs on the results and emits either a green pass or a flagged regression with statistical summary.
- Dashboard panels created and Datadog monitors provisioned with runbook links.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: Implement soak-runner and YAML profiles; run local/in-cluster smoke tests.
- Week 2: Run full suite against staging Dedicated pools, tune warmup and thresholds.
- Week 3: Automate detector + CI gating; run nightly full-soak for 7 days to measure false positives.
- Week 4: Promote monitors and gating to runtime-1.22 release path.

Risks / trade-offs:
- Cost: running 6-hour soaks against Dedicated pools is expensive; mitigate by scheduling runs during off-peak and using smaller test pools where possible.
- False positive sensitivity: tuned detector reduces developer interruption but may miss small regressions; balance set by alpha and threshold parameters.
- Representative traffic: production sampling is required for realism; missing rare tail behaviors could hide regressions.

Next steps / implementation tasks (high level):
- [ ] Implement soak-runner microservice and k8s job templates.
- [ ] Define YAML workload profiles and upload baseline snapshots for current runtime.
- [ ] Add bootstrap-based regression detector and CI GitHub Action.
- [ ] Create Grafana dashboard and Datadog monitors with runbooks.

Artifacts / links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood/company/dedicated-soak-suite
- Example PR (runner): https://github.com/redwood-inference/soak-harness/pull/211
- Baseline snapshots S3 path: s3://redwood-perf/baselines/runtime-1.21/
activity_log: 2026-01-18: Ticket created by Anika Shah. Initial scope and goals added.
2026-01-20: Spike completed - prototype soak-runner can run k6 scripts and push traces to OTLP. Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/soak-harness/pull/198
2026-01-24: Design review with infra and SRE. Decided on 15-minute warmup and EWMA smoothing for detector. Action: SRE to provision staging pool for full soak runs.
2026-01-28: Ran first 6-hour steady soak against staging. Observed tokens/sec steady at 94% of baseline; p95 increased by 12%. Uploaded results to S3 and opened analysis doc.
2026-02-01: Regression detector tuned to reduce false positives after noisy-burst test produced one spurious p95 alert. Thresholds increased and bootstrap sample size doubled.
2026-02-02: PR for CI gating opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/211; assigned reviewers: @marina, @cheng.
acceptance_criteria: Harness runs via k8s job and artifacts are reproducible (logs + Prom + traces).
Nightly soak completes 6-hour steady-state without regression flag for baseline runtime-1.21, or flags are triaged with root cause documented.
Datadog alerts and Grafana dashboard exist with runbook and clear ownership.
CI quick-scan executes on PRs affecting runtime kernels and fails PRs that trigger validated regressions.
